title: How to budget and book a trip to RSA Conference 2027
summary: RSA Conference 2027 at Moscone: SoMa lodging, SFO–BART transfers, FY2027 per diem, Expo pacing, and client dinners in Yerba Buena.
body_markdown:
Four days at Moscone for RSA Conference 2027 can either leave you with a sharper threat-and-vendor shortlist, or a less useful collection of illegible notes, SWAG and an expense report that needs explaining. How well you plan for a successful conference will help ensure it’s the former.


This guide covers useful planning tips for any attendee, from pre-travel budgeting to a post travel debrief, and the logistics in-between


### Key Takeaways


- According to Navan’s 2026 sample data, the median nightly rate was $99 lower for bookings made 2–4 weeks ahead than for those made 1–2 months ahead.
- April’s federal lodging ceiling in San Francisco trails what Moscone-adjacent hotels charged during last year’s RSAC week, so underwrite the gap or trade SoMa for a longer Union Square or FiDi walk.
- From San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) gets you downtown in roughly 30 minutes, often faster than a rideshare stuck in SoMa traffic.
- It can be worth keeping the day to three–four sessions with open blocks for Expo demos and hallway chats that can help evaluate vendors.
- [Navan Edge](https://navan.com/product/navan-edge) can coordinate your SFO flight, Moscone-area hotel, and dinner reservations in one thread.


## What is RSA Conference and who is it for?


RSA Conference (RSAC™ Conference) is the flagship annual cybersecurity conference hosted by RSA Conference LLC. The 2027 edition runs April 5–8 at Moscone Center (North, South, and West halls) in San Francisco.\[1\]\[2\]


The crowd spans CISOs building vendor shortlists, security architects comparing detection stacks, researchers and practitioners exchanging incident playbooks, government and enterprise buyers, and startups launching on the Expo floor. RSAC 2026 drew nearly 44,000 attendees, 700+ speakers across 570+ sessions, and 600+ exhibitors.\[3\]


## What makes RSA Conference 2027 worth the trip


RSAC is where the cybersecurity industry stress-tests strategy before budget season. For practitioners, that means hearing threat research and product demos you can’t recreate from a webinar. For leaders, it means walking the Expo with a prioritized shortlist and the context to say yes or no before another renewal cycle.


The full agenda will be published closer to the event. It’s worth planning for a broad mix of:


- **Keynotes and expert sessions:** Main-stage and deep-dive programming across risk, privacy, AI security, and digital trust\[1\]
- **Technical learning and hands-on experiences:** Labs, sandboxes, and innovation showcases that reward time on the floor, not only in theaters
- **Expo and industry showcase:** Hundreds of vendors and startups will likely be competing for your attention, so bring a focused shortlist
- **After-hours circuit:** Vendor receptions and community meetups typically fill SoMa; lists usually surface closer to the event


The trip is really worth it to leave with three–five vendor conversations that advance an evaluation, a clearer view of what to deploy next, and relationships that extend beyond the week in San Francisco. This is much easier to achieve when all the logistics are taken care of..


## Where to stay for RSA Conference 2027


Hotel location impacts RSAC week as well as your session list. Sleeping a short walk . A quick reset before a client dinner, and an on-time start for early keynotes can make all the difference.

### RSA Conference hotel pricing


Navan’s anonymized analysis of 1,569 hotel bookings near Moscone Center for March 20–27, 2026 found a $744 median nightly rate—about 75% above the $426 median for March 2–8, 2026. Treat that as your April 2027 planning benchmark, then price-check open inventory against any official room block when they open.


- **Nightly benchmark:** The March 20–27, 2026 booking period cleared a $744 median beside Moscone. Pressure-test that figure against your lodging allowance before you commit to a SoMa hotel.
- **Trip length:** The typical business stay ran **3 nights** in **3.9-star** hotels, so underwrite four calendar days of lodging, not one “conference night.”
- **Arrival rhythm:** Monday was the most common check-in day, and Thursday the most common checkout day.
- **Late bookings:** 50% of stays were reserved inside two weeks of check-in, and 31.5% inside seven days—if you’re already in that crunch, shop neighborhoods that still have rooms instead of hoping rates fall.


Booking windows (median nightly rate by how far ahead people reserved):


- **2+ months ahead:** $777 median
- **1–2 months ahead:** $833 median (steepest window—steer around it when you can)
- **2–4 weeks ahead:** $734 median (about **$99** under the 1–2 month spike)
- **1–2 weeks ahead:** $799 median
- **Last minute (0–7 days):** $646 median—lowest on paper, but luck more than a plan when half the market is already hunting scraps


When RSAC publishes official blocks, price-check against public rates the same day. A contracted rate can lose to open inventory, and Moscone-adjacent rooms still book up quickly during cybersecurity week.

## Set your San Francisco budget before traveling


Badge price, flights and hotel rooms are the easy line items. Airport transfers, client dinners, and after-hours networking are some of the things that can be forgotten and then break policy, so map those ahead of time.


### Federal per diem for San Francisco


According to the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) per diem tables, for April under fiscal year 2027, the ceilings are:\[4\]


- **$324 per day** combined ($232 lodging + **$92** M&IE)
- **Inside M&IE:** Breakfast allowance $23; lunch $26; dinner $38; incidentals $5—subtract meals the conference already covers
- **Transit days:** First and last travel days usually pay 75% M&IE ($69) while you’re in motion


GSA rates apply by federal fiscal year; double-check gsa.gov before travel.


### Other expenses to consider


- **Conference registration:** RSAC 2027 pass prices aren’t published on the official registration page at the time of this publication. You can register your interest for $100 off an All Access Pass when registration opens, then verify live prices before you buy.\[5\]
- **Conference-provided meals:** Reduce the M&IE line for those days and note which lunches or receptions your badge covers.\[4\]
- **Airport transfer:** BART from SFO to downtown is typically $11.80 one way; rideshares often run $35–$50+ with surge during peak arrival windows.\[6\]\[7\]
- **Client dinners:** Sit-down SoMa and FiDi dinners often run $75–$150 per person once tax and tip land.
- **After-hours networking buffer:** Vendor receptions may be hosted, but rideshares, cover charges, and late-night surges can still add up.


Total the list before you purchase anything so you’re not rebuilding the week from memory at 35,000 feet.


## How to plan your RSA Conference agenda


It’s tempting to attend as many sessions as possible for fear of missing valuable insight. In reality, attending three or four sessions and leaving some time open for the Expo and hallway track can be just as, or more, impactful.


To date, RSAC has described a program built around keynotes, expert sessions, technical learning, the Expo, and community networking.\[1\]


Plan an agenda that allows you time for:


- **Sessions:** Star must-see talks in the RSAC app or Session Scheduler the day it opens; drop anything you’ll catch in the recording later.
- **Meetings:** Ping vendors, peers, or customers roughly 14 days before wheels-down with a concrete 15-minute ask rather than a vague “let’s connect.”
- **Logistics:** Install the conference app, turn on your out-of-office, and account for movement across the Moscone Center.
- **Contacts:** Pick QR, NFC, or LinkedIn up front, and jot down specific remarks or important context after every useful conversation while it’s still fresh. This will help you be more personal and intentional when following up after the event.


For a broader pre-trip checklist, see[how to plan a business trip](https://navan.com/blog/edge/how-to-plan-a-business-trip) .


## What to pack for RSA Conference 2027


RSAC could be described as sitting somewhere between a research conference and an enterprise sales floor. For business casual pack items like tailored pants/dress or dark denim, a button-down or knit that still looks intentional, comfortable, closed-toe shoes for Expo miles, and a blazer if you’ve got CISO dinners or closed-door forums.


If you’re working on a booth, staff generally lean smart-casual, and presenters should dress one step up from attendees walking the floor.


San Francisco in early April is mild, with highs around the mid-60s °F and lows near 50°F, with cooler evenings.\[8\] Layers work better than a single heavy coat. Note that Moscone rooms run cold even when it feels pleasant outside.


### Conference essentials


- **Two pairs of shoes:** Moscone’s hard floors and North–South–West trek can take a toll. Swapping shoes can help cut the risk of blisters after long Expo days.
- **Portable battery/chargers:** Badge scans, maps, and session alerts can drain a phone by mid-afternoon.
- **Refillable water bottle:** Dry hall air and back-to-back keynotes dehydrate you faster than you notice.
- **Hand sanitizer:** Enclosed halls packed with tens of thousands of people raise the odds of catching the midweek conference cold.
- **Earplugs:** Useful for light sleepers in busy SoMa hotels.
- **Light layer:** A sweater or jacket for over-air-conditioned breakout rooms.


## Getting from the airport to the RSA Conference venue


Most RSAC travelers land at San Francisco International Airport (SFO), roughly 13 miles south of Moscone.\[7\] From SFO, BART runs straight into downtown in roughly 30 minutes; Powell or Montgomery means a short walk or Muni hop to the halls.\[6\]

Solo arrivals in business hours usually do better on BART than in SoMa traffic. Land Sunday if it’s possible so that Monday opens with breakfast and badge collection, instead of recovering from a red-eye.


## Beyond sessions: Make time for the Expo floor and hallway conversations


The best RSAC conversations often start on the Expo floor, in a sandbox demo, or in the five minutes after a keynote when everyone’s still processing the same slide.


- **Use the RSAC app:** Track room changes, capacity, and navigation across Moscone North, South, and West in real time once the app is live for 2027.
- **Work the Expo with a shortlist:** Visit the 10–15 vendors that map to an open evaluation; skip the booth crawl that doesn’t provide you with real value.
- **Protect evening energy:** There will likely be plenty of vendor receptions and community meetups in SoMa after hours. Choose a couple that match your goals instead of simply accepting every invite if doing so will lead to burnout.


## Tips for effective networking


Spontaneous networking can be enjoyable and also effective. If this is less your style, but it’s still an important goal of attending RSAC, treat networking as a before–during–after system:


Before: Build your target list (vendors, peers, customers), skim recent threat or product announcements, and send personalized outreach roughly 14 days before the event with a concrete 15-minute ask.


During: Lead with curiosity (“What are you deploying first against X?”) instead of a product pitch. Introduce colleagues who should meet each other. Capture one line of context per contact immediately.


After (within 48 hours): Email a two-sentence recap of the conversation, suggest one next step, and connect on LinkedIn with that same note. Block a follow-up window on your calendar before departing from SFO.\[9\]


In general, carving some unscheduled time each day to step outside for ten minutes, eat a real lunch, or resetting at the hotel could be beneficial if you know you’ll struggle to remain focused during afternoon scheduling.


## What to eat at RSA Conference 2027


Four days of keynotes and Expo miles call for plenty of fuel. Eat a nutricious breakfast when you can, and keep a protein snack for sessions that run long. For meals in the area:


Client dinner: Fogo de Chão on 3rd Street is located steps from Moscone and handles group and private dining for evaluation dinners that need a table, rather than a standing reception.\[10\]


Team meal: Tropisueño on Yerba Buena Lane is nice for a livelier group dinner a short walk from the halls without white-tablecloth formality.\[11\]


Quick fuel: Yerba Buena Gardens cafés sit between Moscone buildings for coffee and a reset between sessions. Lines within the venue obviously peak at lunch, so perhaps leave five minutes earlier than you anticipate.

## Finish strong on departure day


Being organized on the last day (when you might feel the most tired) can help make sure you don’t leave any important takeaways behind. Here are some helpful tips:


- **Pack the night before:** Charge devices, clear hotel drawers, and stage your badge and laptop by the door, as Thursday checkout near Moscone gets busy.
- **Late checkout:** Ask at check-in and confirm the night before if your flight is evening-bound. Navan Edge can request late checkout on your behalf.
- **Airport buffer:** Aim for at least two hours before a domestic SFO departure and three hours before an international one; post-conference security lines could move slowly.
- **Lounge time:** If your card includes lounge access, use it to organize notes and receipts before you board.
- **Expenses:** File receipts within 48 hours, and flag any out of budget expenses in advance.
- **Schedule a debrief:** Book time on your calendar to share what you learned with your team while it’s top of mind, before you get pulled back into your day-to-day.


## Make your RSA Conference 2027 trip count


RSAC week rewards attendees who treat Moscone like a project with a deadline: Book lodging with eyes open on the premium, leave whitespace in the agenda, and start follow-up before you leave San Francisco. Those choices make it easier to return with a clearer security plan—and fewer surprise charges.
